depth: The monocular depth map shows a continuous depth progression through the indoor studio. It positions two seated people at the extreme left—one wearing a green shirt and mask at approximately 0.4–0.6 m and another in a white shirt directly behind or beside them at approximately 0.8–1.0 m—within the camera wearer's arm's reach. In the lower-right foreground, a low coffee table with a small plant and tissue box is about 1.0–1.5 m away. A man in a black shirt occupies an armchair in the middle ground at approximately 2.2–2.5 m, beside a large potted plant and a collapsible backdrop on his right, also around 2.0–2.5 m away. Throughout the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns their head slightly to the right while the stationary objects retain fixed distances relative to one another. Consequently, the two seated people on the left are increasingly cut off by the left boundary, and a vertical room divider about 2.5 m away at the far right enters the image during frames 3–5. The depth silhouettes indicate that the foreground-left people face forward-right and that the middle-ground man faces forward-right across the table, looking somewhat upward and right instead of directly toward the camera wearer. The coffee table, plant, and tissue box are reachable by both the foreground seated pair and the middle-ground man, whose lower legs are partly hidden behind the tabletop. Relative to the RGB strip alone, the depth visualization distinguishes the overlapping foreground legs, tabletop plane, and middle-ground armchair more clearly as separate metric-depth layers, while emphasizing the nearby intrusion of the right-edge partition in frames 3–5. Its estimates become unreliable beyond approximately 4–5 m in the upper-right background: the garment steamer, vanity area, and two distant people about 5–7 m away—one seated in blue facing left and one standing in black—merge into almost uniform black. Fine leaves on the potted plants are also blurred into solid shapes, and the nearest lower-left person is saturated bright white.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation display separates individual scene objects by category and outline. It identifies the nearest people on the left as `person` instances at approximately 0.4–1.0 m, partly outside the bottom-left of the image; the large left-side `potted plant` at about 2.0 m; the seated middle-ground man as a `person` at approximately 2.2–2.5 m along with his `chair`; and the foreground coffee table as a `dining table` at about 1.0–1.5 m, with a small `potted plant` above it. It also marks the background salon/studio `chair` and two distant `person` instances in the upper right at approximately 5–7 m, around 3–4 m beyond the middle-ground man. The masks depict the middle-ground man sitting upright and facing right or forward-right, rather than toward the camera wearer, with his hands in his lap and his lower legs hidden by the table mask. The distant person dressed in black faces left toward the seated person in blue, who is within their arm's reach. The foreground table and the objects placed on it are reachable by both the foreground and middle-ground seated people. As the camera pans slightly right over the 5 frames, the left-side `person` masks recede farther beyond the left border, the large left `potted plant` mask vanishes entirely in frames 4 and 5, and a distant studio object at the extreme right is newly labelled as a `chair` in those same two frames. Whereas the upper-right people visually merge with dark studio equipment and mirrors in the RGB image, the segmentation output distinctly locates the background people and chairs at approximately 5–7 m as separate instances. Several results are nevertheless unreliable: the tissue box becomes an unlabelled black void within the `dining table` mask and is briefly partly mistaken for a `cup` in frame 1; a `backpack` is hallucinated on the floor in frame 2 and a `book` on the left armrest in frame 3; the two foreground-left people are combined into one `person` mask in frame 1; the white-shirted person's torso is missed in frames 2–4; and the large left `potted plant` is omitted completely from the last two frames.
pose: Against a black background, the body-and-hand pose visualization draws 2D skeletal keypoints. Across all 5 frames, it detects only one yellow upper- and mid-body skeleton, belonging to the black-shirted man seated at approximately 2.2–2.5 m in the center-left. It additionally finds one magenta hand skeleton in frame 1 at roughly 0.5 m in the lower-left foreground, within the camera wearer's immediate reach, corresponding to the crossed arms of the nearest seated person. The yellow head, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip joints indicate that the middle-ground man is seated with his torso turned forward-right. His arms are bent, with both wrists brought together in his lap and within reach of the tabletop edge ahead, while his head cluster points toward his left/forward-right rather than toward the camera wearer. As the viewpoint pans to the right across the 5 frames, the foreground magenta hand disappears after frame 1 because the closest person moves farther beyond the left edge. Meanwhile, the yellow skeleton moves slightly left in image coordinates, and its lower-limb landmarks contract from an incorrectly spread-out leg extension in frame 1 into a compact seated hip-and-thigh arrangement in frames 2–5. In comparison with the RGB strip, where the man's black shirt, dark trousers, and dimly lit armchair blend together, the pose output clearly marks his shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip articulations, as well as the exact finger pose of the foreground hand in frame 1. The map is otherwise highly incomplete and unreliable: it misses the bodies of both foreground seated people at approximately 0.4–1.0 m in every frame, fails to find either distant background person at approximately 5–7 m in the upper right, omits magenta hand skeletons for the middle-ground man even though his hands are visible in his lap, and generates malformed right-leg and knee keypoints in frame 1 where the coffee table blocks his lower legs.
